data.narrative:
Commonwealth Fusion Systems (CFS), a Series B2-stage private company in the Climate & Energy sector, has raised $863M to date. The valuation landscape for CFS is constrained by limited comparable data. While nine peers operate within Climate & Energy, the peer-median method is not applicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables; achieving the minimum three datapoints within narrow filters proved infeasible. The comp universe comprises one public peer (LNZA) and eight private peers including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

Given the absence of reliable peer-median triangulation, no single valuation range can be derived from the standard methodology. The narrow peer set reflects the specialized and capital-intensive nature of frontier energy technologies, where few companies operate at CFS's stage and sector intersection. Any valuation estimate would require supplementary approaches—such as venture capital method, precedent transaction analysis, or DCF modeling with explicit stage-adjusted risk assumptions—none of which are supported by the provided dataset.

Key uncertainties center on the appropriate discount rate for Series B2 capital, long-term technology risk, and regulatory pathway timelines, all of which would materially influence enterprise value. Without broader market data or explicit financial projections, a defensible valuation range cannot be synthesized at this time.
